content.text: {"answer":"The context does not record any test or observation confirming that a minted token was actually verified to work on only one app. What is recorded is the design/implementation: `mintDeployToken` in packages/control-plane/src/fly.js calls Fly's `createLimitedAccessToken` GraphQL mutation with `profile: 'deploy'` and `profileParams: { app_id: flyApp }` plus `expiry: '1h0m0s'` (packages/control-plane/src/fly.js:48-56), and decision d2 states the intent was to scope the token to exactly one app and expire it in 1 hour, motivated by the concern that 'any authenticated user gets credentials for every machine in the org' (m1812). Decision d7 also notes a correction that the mutation required `app_id` rather than `app_name` in profileParams (m2077), which was necessary for the scoping to work as intended — but this is a fix to the request shape, not a reported verification that the resulting token was actually restricted at use-time. No session message or decision cites an observed test (e.g., attempting to deploy a second app with the token and having it rejected) confirming the scope held.
